articles.title: President Droupadi Murmu Pays Tribute to Dr APJ Abdul Kalam on Birth Anniversary
articles.content: Top Stories of the Day Share DD India October 15, 2026 3:52 PM IST President Droupadi Murmu Pays Tribute to Dr APJ Abdul Kalam on Birth Anniversary Author: DD India President Droupadi Murmu on Thursday paid floral tributes to former President Dr APJ Abdul Kalam on his birth anniversary in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh. The President is visiting the city to attend the National SARAS Mela. Born on October 15, 1931, in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu, Dr Avul Pakir Jainulabdeen Abdul Kalam was one of India’s most distinguished scientists and played a significant role in the country’s space and defence programmes. He served as the 11th President of India from July 25, 2002, to July 25, 2007. Dr Kalam graduated in aeronautical engineering from the Madras Institute of Technology. As Project Director, he made a significant contribution to the development of India’s first indigenous Satellite Launch Vehicle, SLV-III, which successfully placed the Rohini satellite into near-Earth orbit in July 1980. He also contributed to the evolution of the Indian Space Research Organisation’s launch vehicle programme, particularly the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle configuration. After working with ISRO for around two decades, Dr Kalam joined the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), where he led the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme. He played a key role in the development and operationalisation of the Agni and Prithvi missile systems, strengthening India’s indigenous defence capabilities. From July 1992 to December 1999, he served as Scientific Adviser to the Defence Minister and Secretary of the Department of Defence Research and Development. During this period, he contributed to the development of strategic missile systems and the Pokhran-II nuclear tests in collaboration with the Department of Atomic Energy. He also supported efforts to promote self-reliance in defence technologies, including projects such as the Light Combat Aircraft. Dr Kalam received several prestigious honours during his lifetime, including the Padma Bhushan in 1981, the Padma Vibhushan in 1990 and the Bharat Ratna, India’s highest civilian award, in 1997. He was also conferred honorary doctorates by 30 universities and institutions. Beyond science and public service, Dr Kalam inspired generations through his writings and vision for India’s development. His books, including Wings of Fire, India 2020: A Vision for the New Millennium, My Journey and Ignited Minds: Unleashing the Power Within India, have been widely read in India and abroad and translated into several Indian languages. As President, Dr Kalam emphasised transforming India into a developed nation by 2020. Remembered as the “People’s President”, he continues to be recognised for his contributions to science, education and national development.

articles.title: Vishvajit More Wins India's First U23 Greco-Roman Silver - GKToday
articles.content: Home Vishvajit More Wins India’s First U23 Greco-Roman Silver Vishvajit More Wins India’s First U23 Greco-Roman Silver October 15, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 Indian wrestler Vishvajit Ramchandra More won silver in the men’s 55kg Greco-Roman event at the U23 World Wrestling Championships on 15 October 2026. He became the first Indian wrestler to win a Greco-Roman silver medal at the U23 championships. The final took place in Las Vegas, United States, where More lost 12–13 to Georgia’s Koba Karumidze. Final and Route to the Medal More reached the final after defeating Iran’s U20 World Champion Shamsipour 8–1 in the quarter-finals and Russia’s Malik Gigiev 7–4 in the semi-finals. The narrow one-point margin in the final gave Karumidze the gold medal and More the silver. More’s silver was India’s first medal at the 2026 U23 World Wrestling Championships. It was also his third medal at the competition: he had won bronze in 2024 in Albania and in 2025 in Serbia. Greco-Roman Wrestling Greco-Roman wrestling is an international wrestling style in which holds and attacks below the waist are prohibited. Wrestlers use their upper bodies to execute holds, throws and other legal techniques. Freestyle wrestling is another internationally contested style and permits attacks on the legs. The 55kg category is a weight class in which competitors must meet the applicable weight limit at the official weigh-in. The United World Wrestling (UWW) governs international wrestling and organises world championships across age groups and styles. U23 Championships and Indian Participation The U23 World Wrestling Championships are an international competition for wrestlers in the under-23 age category. The 2026 championships were held in Las Vegas. India’s participation faced visa difficulties, with nine wrestlers from the Greco-Roman and women’s categories denied United States visas. Important Facts for Exams Greco-Roman wrestling prohibits holds and attacks below the waist. United World Wrestling is the international governing body for wrestling. Vishvajit More won U23 World Championships bronze medals in 2024 and 2025 before taking silver in 2026. More’s 2026 final against Koba Karumidze ended 13–12. The 2026 U23 World Wrestling Championships took place in Las Vegas, United States. More competed in the men’s 55kg Greco-Roman event. articles.title: PM Modi Inaugurates Rs 3350 Crore Development Projects in Ladakh - Pragativadi
articles.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi virtually inaugurated and dedicated five major development projects worth around ₹3,350 crore in Ladakh on Thursday, marking a major milestone in strengthening the Union Territory’s infrastructure, regional connectivity, energy security, and cultural preservation. Addressing the citizens of Ladakh, the Prime Minister highlighted the central government’s commitment to driving sustainable development in the high-altitude region while safeguarding its fragile ecology and empowering local youth. Key Projects Dedicated to the Nation The ₹3,350 crore developmental package covers critical sectors ranging from civil aviation to high-altitude water management: New Terminal at Leh Airport: Built at a cost of ₹650 crore, the new terminal at the Kushok Bakula Rinpoche Airport expands annual passenger capacity from 10 lakh to 35 lakh. Notably, it stands as India’s first airport terminal equipped with geothermal heating alongside solar power systems designed to withstand harsh winter conditions. Nimmu–Padum–Darcha Road Corridor: Constructed at ₹2,500 crore, this vital strategic road drastically reduces travel time across key regional routes from 12 hours down to just 3 hours, offering a crucial boost to trade, logistics, and local commerce. Hanu Hydroelectric Project & Power Grid: The Prime Minister dedicated the Hanu hydroelectric plant along with its associated transmission network, enhancing power reliability across remote rural settlements. Project Amrit Him Sarovar: PM Modi dedicated 40 newly constructed high-altitude reservoirs designed to store water and ensure irrigation security for farmers during critical agricultural cycles. Petroglyph Conservation Park: To preserve the region’s ancient heritage, India’s first dedicated Petroglyph Conservation Park was inaugurated in Leh to protect prehistoric rock art. Empowering Youth and Local Economy Highlighting the territorial expansion achieved since Ladakh became a Union Territory in 2019, PM Modi noted that the road network has expanded from 1,800 km to over 4,000 km, while tap water coverage has surged from 3.5% to nearly 99% of households. To boost local higher education and stem youth migration, the Prime Minister announced the establishment of a Center of Excellence in Leh alongside satellite campus proposals for IIT Jammu and IIM Jammu. He also reiterated support for local GI-tagged products, including Pashmina, sea-buckthorn, and Ladakhi apricots, on global commercial platforms. articles.title: Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train: 371 Km Of Viaduct Completed, Over 9,300 OHE Masts Installed
articles.content: Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor (Pic Via NHSRCL) The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project has recorded significant construction progress, with 371 km of viaduct construction completed as of September 2026, according to the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL), the implementing agency for India's first bullet train corridor. According to NHSRCL, apart from the viaduct construction, 456 km of pier work, alongside 18 river bridges and 16 steel bridges have been completed on the 508-km bullet train corridor. Additionally, noise barriers have been installed along 301 km of the alignment to minimise operational noise. Track-related infrastructure has also advanced, with 98 km of track linking completed. Meanwhile, more than 9,300 overhead equipment (OHE) masts have been installed across 206 km, marking progress towards electrification. In Maharashtra, excavation of four mountain tunnels has been completed, while 5 km of tunnelling using the New Austrian Tunnelling Method (NATM) has been achieved. The project, being developed with Japanese technical and financial assistance, is designed to support high-speed train operations at speeds of up to 320 kmph. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had earlier said that the construction of the Vapi-Surat section of the corridor is targeted for completion by December 2026, after which testing and associated works will follow. The Surat-Bilimora section is expected to become the first operational stretch of the corridor in 2027. Work is also progressing on India’s indigenously developed high-speed train. The first body frame has been completed and is undergoing structural testing, while the train is expected to begin track trials by May-June 2027. The corridor, which is India's first bullet train project, will connect Mumbai and Ahmedabad through 12 stations across Maharashtra, Gujarat and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had earlier announced that India’s first bullet train will begin its inaugural 100-km run between Surat and Vapi in August 2027, The New Indian Express reported . The section is part of the larger 508-km Mumbai–Ahmedabad high-speed corridor, also known as Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project, which is expected to be fully operational by 2029. Vaishnaw said the Mumbai–Ahmedabad travel time would drop to 1 hour 58 minutes once the corridor is ready. He added that the first operational run in August 2027 would be limited to the 100-km Surat–Vapi stretch. "A significant milestone is that the bullet train will cover the distance between Ahmedabad and Mumbai in just 1 hour 58 minutes upon the completion of the high-speed rail corridor. The inaugural run in August 2027 will cover 100 km between Surat and Vapi," Vaishaw said. The minister said trains on the 508-km corridor will operate at speeds of up to 320 kmph. With four stops, the Mumbai–Ahmedabad trip will take 1 hour 58 minutes, while halting at all 12 stations will extend the journey to 2 hours 17 minutes. articles.title: ARAI becomes India's first test agency to offer integrated vehicle cybersecurity services
articles.content: Auto Technology 1 min read ARAI becomes India's first test agency to offer integrated vehicle cybersecurity services Facility offers testing, validation, R&D and homologation, including assessments for compliance with AIS-189 and AIS-190 standards ETAuto Desk ETAuto Published On Oct 15, 2026 at 11:49 AM IST Select ETAuto as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook As vehicles become increasingly connected and software-defined, cybersecurity has become a critical part of vehicle safety, technology development and regulatory compliance. The Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) has become the country's first test agency to offer integrated vehicle cybersecurity testing, verification, validation, research and development (R&D), and homologation services, the organisation said on Wednesday. The services bring cybersecurity assessment and development capabilities under one roof, enabling vehicle manufacturers and component suppliers to evaluate and address cyber risks across vehicle platforms in India, according to an official press release. Advt The facility supports compliance with AIS-189, which covers Cyber Security Management Systems, and AIS-190, relating to Software Update Management Systems. It also extends beyond these regulatory requirements through advanced cybersecurity research, development and validation services. As vehicles become increasingly connected and software-defined, cybersecurity has become a critical part of vehicle safety, technology development and regulatory compliance. ARAI's integrated offering is aimed at helping manufacturers assess vulnerabilities and strengthen the security of connected vehicle systems throughout their development and operational lifecycle. Beyond regulatory compliance In addition to AIS-189 and AIS-190 compliance-related assessments, ARAI has developed facilities for XiL-based cybersecurity evaluation and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) testing. Its services include Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT), verification and validation of Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA) reports, development of Hardware Security Modules (HSM) and Software Security Modules (SSM), and tracking and maintenance of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) records. The facility can assess vehicles, electronic control units, connected systems and other automotive electronic components against potential cyber threats and vulnerabilities. Advt By combining testing, R&D, verification, validation and homologation, ARAI aims to support manufacturers and suppliers from the vehicle development stage through lifecycle support. The development is also expected to strengthen India's domestic capabilities in advanced automotive technologies by providing the industry with infrastructure to undertake specialised cybersecurity assessments within the country, reducing the need to seek such services overseas. articles.title: Union Cabinet approves Rs 2,000 crore bonus for 11 lakh railway staff
articles.content: NEW DELHI: THE Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Wednesday approved a productivity-linked bonus (PLB) equivalent to 78 days’ wages worth Rs 2,009.61 crore to around 11 lakh railway employees ahead of the festive season. Payment of PLB to eligible railway employees is made each year before the Dussehra and Diwali holidays. The Cabinet also extended the National Social Assistance Programme for another five years till 2030-31, with an outlay of Rs 53,428 crore. The programme will be renamed the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana. Under the revised provisions, monthly assistance under the disability pension scheme will be Rs 375 for beneficiaries aged up to 79 years and Rs 625 for those above 80 years. The minimum benchmark disability requirement will be reduced from 80% to 40%. As part of the restructuring of the social welfare programmes, the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme has been renamed to Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana and the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme to Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana. Similarly, the Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme will be known as Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana and the National Family Benefit Scheme will become the Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana. articles.title: IBM to install India's first quantum computer in Amaravati in early 2027 for post-quantum cryptography
articles.content: Home Trending News IBM to install India’s first quantum computer in Amaravati in early 2027 for post-quantum cryptography IBM to install India’s first quantum computer in Amaravati in early 2027 for post-quantum cryptography IBM plans to deploy India’s largest quantum computer as part of the Andhra Pradesh Quantum Valley initiative backed by Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu. By Ishita Ganguly 14 Oct 2026 Follow Us New Update IBM to install India’s first quantum computer IBM plans to deploy India’s largest quantum computer early next year at the newly developed tech park in Amaravati, a top executive said. IBM to install India’s first quantum computer in Amaravati in early 2027 The facility will develop practical applications for quantum computing and help Indian enterprises prepare their IT infrastructure for post-quantum cryptography. “I think the facility is almost ready… Machines here early next year,” said Sandip Patel, Managing Director. Advertisment Add Startup Pedia As A Trusted Source A part of the Andhra Pradesh Quantum Valley initiative backed by Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu, IBM is working with Tata Consultancy Services (TCS). A supercomputer uses regular computing technology and works with bits that store information as 0 or 1. It can process large amounts of data and perform complex calculations, used for weather forecasts, space research and climate studies. Meanwhile, a quantum computer uses quantum bits, called qubits, to solve certain complex problems differently. Scientists are now studying how it can help develop new medicines, or discover materials and solve difficult scientific problems. Also read: UAE-based LuLu Group makes Chennai debut with 1 lakh sq. ft hypermarket, India’s first and largest one within a metro station What is a quantum computer? A quantum computer uses the principles of quantum mechanics, such as superposition and entanglement, to process information in ways that classical computers cannot, potentially solving certain problems exponentially faster. Combining maths, physics and computer science, a quantum computer can solve complex problems. It can also completely transform how we communicate and protect information online. A link between quantum systems is called entanglement. Even when these systems are apart, their states can be connected specially. The National Quantum Mission supports research and development in four main areas - quantum computing, quantum communication, quantum sensing and measurement and quantum materials and devices. Quantum computers could help solve problems related to financial risk, investment planning and managing portfolios. It can also be used in artificial intelligence (AI), assisting quantum machine learning. IBM’s quantum computers are cloud‑accessible superconducting‑qubit systems, including the latest IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 and Nighthawk 120‑qubit processors. These are designed to deliver higher circuit throughput and support real‑world quantum workloads. According to NITI Aayog, India will need to train around 1 lakh quantum computing developers to become a leader in this field in the 2030s. "Real-world quantum applications are still 3-5 years away, but the work on specific uses is progressing globally," IBM’s Sandip Patel said.
